subject: Nimbus private cluster: landing zone, machine-classing, and PV binding strategy
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex@cumulus.tech>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy: k8s landing zone guidance request

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our infra team is starting the procurement and racks work for our first on-prem cluster (Nimbus) and we need a pragmatic landing-zone guide from Redwood for: machine classes, storage binding choices (RWO vs RWX), PVC binding mode, and GPU affinity. We have a short window before procurement sign-off (2 weeks). Attached is a csv with our tentative node class SKUs and a quick NVMe vs SATA plan.

High level constraints:
- 8 racks across two data halls (3+5)
- Mixed GPU+CPU nodes (A100 equivalent + 2x 64-core CPU nodes for actors)
- Local NVMe for ephemeral tensors, network NFS/CSI-backed for durable model shards
- Must meet SOC2 evidence requirements (encryption in transit at minimum; KMS integration TBD)

Can Redwood share recommended node roles, taint/toleration patterns, PV-binding mode for heavy inference pods, and any runbook checks we should include for preflight? Open to a short 30-minute design review.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Senior Platform Lead, Cumulus

Attachments: nimbus-nodetypes.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@cumulus.tech>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy: k8s landing zone guidance request

Alex — thanks for the context and the SKU file. Looping in Marissa (onprem lead), Aditya (runtime/serving), and Laura (security/compliance) so we can put together a focused design doc and a preflight checklist you can use for procurement.

Quick answers up front:
- Machine classes: split into 4 profiles: control-plane (3x HA masters), compute-gpu (A100-class w/ 1 GPU per server for predictable scheduling), compute-cpu (worker nodes for background/actor jobs), infra-storage (higher-capacity SATA with dual controllers for RWX PVs). We'll capture vCPU/mem/disk sizes in the doc.
- PV binding: recommend CSI driver (e.g., portworx/rook/csi provided by partner) and PVC "WaitForFirstConsumer" for zone-aware binding when you rely on local NVMe to be close to pod. For shared model shards RWX backed by Ceph/NFS, use Immediate only if you have stable placement and don't require topology aware binding.
- Ephemeral NVMe: schedule via local-storage class and use Pod annotation to mount ephemeral directories; avoid relying on local for durable checkpoints.
- Taints/tolerations & node selectors: GPU nodes should be tainted gpu=true:NoSchedule; inference pods get toleration and nodeSelector gpu:true. Actor/background pods can land on cpu pool. Use topologyKeys and PodTopologySpread to balance across halls.

Requested from you:
1) Confirm preferred CSI (you listed "in-house CSI" in the CSV — if that's accurate we need driver version and feature parity with CSI spec 1.3).
2) Any hard SLA on failover window for model-serving pods (e.g., 60s, 5m)? that drives replication and PV placement.
3) Compliance: do you expect customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed integration (we can operate with either but the evidence for SOC2 differs).

I've attached a quick disk benchmark we ran against two reference SKUs and a draft runbook template. Can your ops folks do a short sync Wed 10am PT? If that doesn't work, propose two slots.

—Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attachments: disk-io-benchmark.pdf, redwood-onprem-runbook-draft.md

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy: k8s landing zone guidance request

All — quick notes before the call:

1) Preflight checklist (we'll flesh out):
   - Node inventory + rack mapping (CSV good)
   - Firmware matrix + NIC drivers (need for SR-IOV / RDMA if provided)
   - Network egress policy and NAT for model downloads (which registry, any private mirrors?)
   - CSI operator install order and service account permissions (ops team should grant cluster-admin for install window)
   - Backup retention for model shards (object-store target or offsite replication)

2) Storage decisions:
   - Durable model shards: Ceph/Rook recommended for RWX with encryption-at-rest (KMS integration). If you have strict performance SLAs, provide separate high-throughput NVMe-backed block devices mirrored with asynchronous replication.
   - PVC binding mode: default to WaitForFirstConsumer for compute-gpu pods to preserve zone locality. For control-plane and infra services (metrics, logging) Immediate is fine.

3) Scheduling:
   - Use taints gpu=true:NoSchedule, and a lightweight Admission Hook that enforces resource-limits on inference pods (prevents noisy neighbors).
   - Batching/throughput pods: run specialized horizontal-pod-autoscaler using custom metrics from our runtime. We'll provide the HPA template.

I'll put a brief doc together tonight and Aditya can sketch a node role map during Wed's sync.

Marissa
Sr. Manager, On-Prem Deployments — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Chen <alex@cumulus.tech>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@cumulus.tech, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy: k8s landing zone guidance request

Karthik / Marissa — thanks, this is helpful. Wed 10am PT works for our ops lead and me.

Quick clarifications from our side:
- CSI: we're planning to ship with Rook/Ceph v16; ops will paste the operator manifests on the call.
- SLA: initial target is 5m cold restart for model-serving pods; ideally 90% of traffic served without fallbacks during HA events.
- KMS: customer-managed HSM planned, but we can document both approaches; SOC2 evidence will be customer-managed.

I'll bring the rack-level power plan and NIC firmware matrix to the meeting. Please share the draft runbook ahead of the call so we can annotate.

Alex Chen
Senior Platform Lead, Cumulus
